solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Way of life after getting into the habit?

definitions.text: Way of life after getting into the habit?

parts.words: Way of life after getting into the habit?
parts.note: getting into the habit is read literally as putting on a monk's or nun's robe, so the way of life is that of the cloister

explanation.walkthrough: 'Getting into the habit' sounds like forming a routine, but a habit is also the robe worn by monks and nuns.
explanation.definitionFit: Monastic life, the regime of monks and nuns, begins when one takes the religious robe.

clue.text: Open's settled on tee

parts.note: a matter that is settled is over, finished
tee is the spelt-out name of the letter T

explanation.surface: A golf commentator notes that the Open championship was decided at the tee.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Open' looks like the golf championship, but it is the definition, an adjective; the 's is 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Something overt is done openly, not concealed: a synonym.

clue.text: Unending craving for drug

indicators.note: unending tells us to drop the final letter of the word for craving

parts.note: craving something is aspiring to it

explanation.surface: An addict's endless longing for a narcotic.
explanation.definitionFit: Aspirin is a common painkilling medicine, an example of a drug.

clue.text: Ethnic test about Britain

indicators.note: about means the word for test goes round the abbreviation

parts.note: a trial is a test
B is the abbreviation for Britain, as on car plates (GB)

explanation.surface: A survey testing the ethnic make-up of Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: Tribal describes a people grouped by shared descent, close in sense to ethnic.

clue.text: Ocean swirls over first one in kayak

indicators.note: in a down clue, over puts the first piece above the second
the ocean's letters swirl around into a new order

parts.note: 1st, written IST, is the abbreviation for first

explanation.surface: A paddler is caught in swirling ocean water for the first time.
explanation.definitionFit: A canoeist is someone paddling a canoe, and a kayak is a kind of canoe.

clue.text: Tax period

definitions.meaning: to tax someone's abilities is to strain or extend them
a spell of time, or a prison sentence

explanation.definitionFit: Stretch means both to tax one's resources and a continuous period of time.

clue.text: Throttling, giving a signal to turn around

indicators.note: around signals that the letters of the preceding words are moved round into a new order

explanation.surface: A motorist is half-strangled by someone signalling for a U-turn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turn' looks like the anagram signal but is fodder; 'around' is the indicator and 'giving' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Strangulation is choking by squeezing the throat, which is what throttling means.

clue.text: Single politician's over getting threatened

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one, a single
MP is a Member of Parliament, a politician; the 's means 'is'
something over has ended

explanation.surface: A lone MP's career is finished after being threatened.
explanation.definitionFit: Impended means loomed or hung menacingly overhead, as a threat does.

clue.text: Foundation stone in Blenheim sat askew

indicators.note: in places the abbreviation for stone inside the rearranged letters
askew means the letters of the words before it are set crooked, out of order

parts.note: ST is the abbreviation for stone, the British unit of weight

explanation.surface: A foundation stone at Blenheim Palace sits crookedly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'askew' turns BLENHEIM SAT into EABLIHMENT around which ST goes. Blenheim Palace is a stately home in Oxfordshire.
explanation.definitionFit: An establishment is an institution founded, a synonym of foundation in that sense.

clue.text: Tenor with power covering Queen. Idiot …

parts.note: T is the abbreviation for tenor in music

indicators.note: covering means the letters for with and power enclose the Queen

parts.note: P is the abbreviation for power in physics
ER is Elizabeth Regina, the Queen

explanation.surface: A powerful tenor sings over the Queen, the fool.
explanation.definitionFit: A twerp is a silly, annoying person, an informal word for an idiot.

clue.text: … halfwit revealed by design or amusement

indicators.note: revealed by says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Continuing the previous clue, a dimwit gives himself away by his plans or pastimes.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis joins this to 10 across for the surface only.
explanation.definitionFit: An ignoramus is an ignorant person, close in sense to a dimwit or fool.

clue.text: Every other bird in a former embrace

indicators.note: embrace means the word for former wraps round the bird

parts.note: late means former, as in the late president
the tern is a seabird

explanation.surface: A bird lies in the arms of an ex-lover, one after another.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is a link here; 'embrace' does the containing.
explanation.definitionFit: Alternate days are every second day, so the adjective means every other.

clue.text: Greek character, goddess embodying first of Titans

indicators.note: embodying means the goddess takes the letter into her body

parts.note: Thea, or Theia, is a Titaness of Greek myth

indicators.note: first of picks the opening letter of Titans

explanation.surface: A Greek goddess personifies the leading Titan.
explanation.definitionFit: Theta is the eighth letter of the Greek alphabet.

clue.text: Broad giving needle in silence

indicators.note: in puts the needle inside the word for silence

parts.note: to gag someone is to silence them
a pin is a fine needle

explanation.surface: A needle is pushed into someone to keep them quiet, wide open.
explanation.definitionFit: A gaping hole is wide open, broad.

clue.text: Pedestrian way state overturned poor

parts.note: a path is a way for walkers

indicators.note: overturned means the word for state is turned upside down, read upwards

parts.note: to cite is to state or quote

explanation.surface: A footpath in a poor state.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pedestrian' wants to be the definition, meaning dull; it belongs to PATH. 'overturned' gives ETIC.
explanation.definitionFit: A pathetic effort is a poor, feeble one.

clue.text: Lops head off plant

indicators.note: off signals the letters go off into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A gardener lops the top off a plant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'head off' looks like an instruction to drop a first letter, but 'head' is fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Asphodel is a lily-like flowering plant.

clue.text: Disapprove of endlessly strong husband grabbing rear

indicators.note: grabbing means the first letters seize the rear
endlessly removes the last letter of the word for strong

parts.note: hard means strong, tough
the rump is the rear

explanation.surface: A wife disapproves of her strong husband for grabbing her bottom.
explanation.definitionFit: To harrumph is to clear one's throat in pompous disapproval.

clue.text: 'On the Beach' is prosaic for the audience

indicators.note: for the audience means the word is heard by listeners rather than read

parts.note: literal means prosaic, matter-of-fact

explanation.surface: A critic calls the novel On the Beach prosaic.
explanation.walkthrough: On the Beach is a Nevil Shute novel; the quotes disguise a plain phrase meaning by the shore.
explanation.definitionFit: Littoral means of or on the seashore, so a shore-side location.

clue.text: Bird in Sun a lot, rolling over

indicators.note: over turns the concealed run backwards, read upwards in this down clue
in says the letters are concealed inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: A bird rolls over and over, sunbathing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rolling' looks like the reversal signal but supplies RO; 'over' does the reversing.
explanation.definitionFit: The ortolan is a small European bunting, once eaten as a delicacy.

clue.text: Sailor is catching case of dengue and survives

parts.note: AB is an able seaman, a sailor

indicators.note: catching means is holds the letters within it
the case of a word is its outer letters

explanation.surface: A sailor catches dengue fever and lives through it.
explanation.definitionFit: To abide is to endure or last, so abides means survives.

clue.text: Halves portions, taking little time

indicators.note: taking means the portions take in the short time

parts.note: bits are portions
sec, short for second, is a little time

explanation.surface: Someone halves food portions while eating little.
explanation.definitionFit: To bisect something is to cut it into two halves.

clue.text: Ring around ring's centre like part of conifer

indicators.note: around means the peal goes around the central letters

parts.note: a peal is a ringing of bells

indicators.note: the centre of the word ring is its middle two letters

explanation.surface: A ring encircles the centre of a pine tree's trunk.
explanation.definitionFit: Pineal means shaped like a pine cone, the fruit of a conifer.

clue.text: River Test finally divided

indicators.note: finally picks the last letter of Test

parts.note: rent means torn apart, divided

explanation.surface: The River Test is at last split in two.
explanation.walkthrough: The Test is itself a Hampshire river, which makes it look like the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The Trent is a major river of the English Midlands.

clue.text: Terrible shower seek solutions, losing head

indicators.note: losing head means the first letter is dropped

parts.note: to brainstorm is to seek solutions by group discussion

explanation.surface: A terrible downpour hinders people looking for answers.
explanation.definitionFit: A rainstorm is a heavy, unpleasant downpour.

clue.text: Drug of poppy in use medicinally, initially

indicators.note: initially picks the first letter of each of the five words

explanation.surface: A drug made from the poppy is used in medicine.
explanation.definitionFit: Opium is the narcotic extracted from the opium poppy.

clue.text: Standard of France in ruined memorial

indicators.note: in places the abbreviation inside the rearranged letters
ruined means memorial is broken up into a new order

parts.note: F is the international abbreviation for France

explanation.surface: A French flag lies amid a ruined memorial.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ruined' gives ORILAMME, with F inserted. The oriflamme was the royal battle standard of medieval France, so 'Standard of France' fits the surface too.
explanation.definitionFit: The oriflamme was the red banner of the French kings, a standard or flag.

clue.text: Pile of stones roughly hard, not old

parts.note: ca, for circa, means roughly

indicators.note: not means the letter for old is removed

parts.note: iron is very hard

explanation.surface: A heap of stones, hard though not very old.
explanation.definitionFit: A cairn is a mound of stones raised as a marker or memorial.

clue.text: Harmful French article, 'Females almost embracing depressions'

parts.note: un is the French indefinite article

indicators.note: embracing means the shortened word wraps around the depressions
almost drops the final letter

parts.note: women are females
holes are depressions in the ground

explanation.surface: A French newspaper article describes women suffering from depression.
explanation.definitionFit: Unwholesome means bad for health or morals, therefore harmful.
